slides.title: First words and greetings
slides.slide: L1 Basic · First words and greetings
slides.notes: Greet someone, give your name and count to ten in French. Notes: teach Bonjour (hello) and Je m'appelle... (my name is...) with a smile and gesture; learners greet five classmates and say their own name, with no reading or writing needed yet.

slides.title: Sounds, spelling and simple phrases
slides.slide: L2 Awareness · Sounds, spelling and simple phrases
slides.notes: Pronounce common French sounds and read short phrases about family, colours and food. Notes: show that final consonants are often silent, as in petit (small); learners read ten word cards aloud, then match each to a picture.

slides.title: Present tense and simple sentences
slides.slide: L3 Foundation · Present tense and simple sentences
slides.notes: Write and say ten sentences about yourself using regular verbs and the verbs être (to be) and avoir (to have). Notes: give a gap-fill on Je suis... and J'ai...; learners complete it with their own details and swap with a partner to check agreement.

slides.title: Past and future in conversation
slides.slide: L4 Practitioner · Past and future in conversation
slides.notes: Talk about yesterday and next week using the passé composé and the near future. Notes: model J'ai mangé (I ate) and Je vais manger (I am going to eat); learners interview a partner for three minutes, then write six sentences in the past and the future.

slides.title: Argument, texts and accuracy
slides.slide: L5 Specialist · Argument, texts and accuracy
slides.notes: Write a 250-word opinion piece and summarise an authentic article, using the subjunctive where needed. Notes: practise Il faut que je parte (I must leave); learners mark every verb in their draft, fix agreement errors, and defend one opinion in a spoken minute.

slides.title: Literature, linguistics and style
slides.slide: L6 Advanced · Literature, linguistics and style
slides.notes: Analyse a literary or media text for style, register and historical context, and write a critical essay in French. Notes: choose one page of prose; learners find three stylistic choices, compare them with a modern translation, and argue in 600 words which reading is stronger.

slides.title: Research, translation and teaching
slides.slide: L7 Super expert · Research, translation and teaching
slides.notes: Plan and carry out an original piece of French-language research or translation with a documented method. Notes: choose a narrow question, such as how one word's meaning has shifted; collect twenty sources, code them, write up findings in French, and submit them for peer review.
